target_customer: Consumers who want to give away or sell used goods and get items for free, paid for in site credits rather than cash
problem: Giving away or selling unwanted items on Craigslist was slow, produced floods of emails and no-shows, and eBay charged fees.
business_model: Credit-based auction marketplace; credits earned by activity or bought, later point and fee changes and a crypto token experiment

founders.name: Gee-Hwan Chuang
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO with no biography; prior employers and education not found in an opened source.

founders.name: James Fong
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in a company quote (Shareable and press profiles); his failed attempt to give away snowboard boots on Craigslist is the stated origin of the idea.

competitors.name: Freenapkin
competitors.what: Rival give-away-stuff site that publicly claimed ownership of the idea of giving junk away

competitors.name: Craigslist
competitors.what: Dominant classifieds site where free items were already given away, the pain point Listia targeted

technical_complexity.rationale: A web auction with a credit ledger and ratings; standard engineering for a small team, with fraud and moderation as the main hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Two-sided liquidity of buyers and sellers gives some network effect, but rivals such as Freenapkin copied the idea within days and the credit mechanic was easy to imitate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying Listia; local used-goods apps later grew around it.

market_need_then: Craigslist giveaways produced mass emails and no-show winners (TechCrunch, 2009); a free auction with credits offered a cleaner way to dispose of unwanted goods.

identity.logo: Wordmark logo; not described by an opened source
identity.visual_style: Consumer marketplace site with free-stuff tagline
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly consumer pitch: sell your old stuff, get new stuff you love

branding.brand_signature: Free auctions paid in points or credits
branding.community_and_virality: Site claims over 10 million members; no merch or fan culture found.

brand_strength.rationale: Site claims 10 million members and gets consumer press, but no source shows the name itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Listia launched with the Summer 2009 batch with a credit-based free-auction model, raised a $9M Series A from General Catalyst in October 2013 on a mobile push, and is still operating with a claimed 10 million members. It stayed a mid-sized consumer marketplace rather than a breakout, with no exit found. Its later crypto token experiment is noted by press but not dated here.
notes: Total raised reported as 10.77M (CB Insights), 11.17M (TechCrunch via TheCompanyCheck), 9.42M (Seedtable); the recorded rounds sum to about 11.4M so amounts are approximate. The 15K YC amount rests on Seedtable alone. The 400K angel and about 2M seed have no exact dates; the seed amount comes from FinSMEs recapping prior funding. Wikipedia and CB Insights disagree on launch details. No outcome event found.
